Name: PADDR[6:2]
Structural Path: PADDR[6:2] -> s_apb_addr -> PADDIR/GPIOLOCK decode -> protected-write acceptance -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` supplies the address decode that distinguishes `REG_PADDIR` from the other GPIO registers. An attacker can alter `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` during an otherwise valid APB write so that a transaction intended for another register is decoded as `REG_PADDIR`. The supporting RTL chain is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. The presented `PWDATA` is captured into `r_gpio_dir`, changing pad directions without the intended direction-register access.
Justification: Attacker-controlled address bits select the direction register; the de-aliased address path was dynamically controllable.

Name: PWDATA[0]
Structural Path: PWDATA[0] -> GPIOLOCK write data -> r_gpio_lock[0] -> PADDIR authorization -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` carries the direction bitmap selected by the lock check immediately before `r_gpio_dir <= pwdata_l`. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. Once a PADDIR write is admitted, controlling `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` substitutes attacker-selected input/output directions. Pins are configured as outputs or inputs contrary to the authorized software value.
Justification: The untrusted APB write-data bit directly determines the unauthorized direction value.

Name: r_gpio_lock[0]
Structural Path: r_gpio_lock[0] -> PADDIR write authorization -> r_gpio_dir -> gpio_dir
Attack Mechanisms: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` selects whether `PWDATA` or zero is assigned to `pwdata_l` in the PADDIR case. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. Clearing `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` before the access bypasses the lock and lets attacker-controlled `PWDATA` reach `r_gpio_dir`. The lock policy no longer preserves the authorized pad-direction configuration.
Justification: The lock state is controllable through evaluated bus paths and gates whether a direction write is authorized.
